name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Monday 6 January 1992 (English cryptic)

clue.text: Local magistrate's about turn to awfully evil pursuit as rain maker

indicators.note: the magistrate's initials go round, or about, the next piece
something done awfully is done badly, so the following words come out in a jumbled order

blocks.note: a JP, Justice of the Peace, is a local lay magistrate
a U-turn, so U stands for a turn
the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A small-town magistrate abandons the bench for some wicked scheme to make it rain.
explanation.walkthrough: A JP is a Justice of the Peace, an unpaid local magistrate, and a U-turn gives U; the magistrate's initials wrap that turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter Pluvius is the Roman god in his aspect as sender of rain, so he is the bringer of showers.

clue.text: Evangelist tans himself, lying in tomb

definitions.note: a phrase describing the subject of the song, who lies mouldering in the grave

blocks.note: St John is one of the four Gospel writers
the sun browns, or tans, the skin
his body is the man himself, in physical form

explanation.surface: A preacher sunbathes while lying on a sepulchre.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer comes from the marching song: 'John Brown's body lies a-mouldering in the grave'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American Civil War song, the abolitionist's corpse lies in the grave, so the remains are what lies entombed.

clue.text: Be proud of what one hopes to do?

blocks.note: first meaning: to stand out from a surface, as proud is used of something raised
second meaning: a planned undertaking, the scheme one intends to carry out

explanation.walkthrough: Proud looks like pride in an achievement; in joinery and medicine proud means sticking out above the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to jut out, and as a noun it is a scheme or planned enterprise one aims to complete.

clue.text: Transmitted and printed by Lawrence, deeply disturbed about model

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown out of order, so the word before it is rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters wrap the model

blocks.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, by his initials
taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A message is sent and printed by Lawrence, who is badly upset about a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: TE comes first, then the anagram of deeply wrapped round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A teletype machine sends typed messages down a line and prints them at the other end, so teletyped means sent and printed.

clue.text: Pharaoh, Egypt's leader, in confusion following guns

indicators.note: in puts the leading letter inside the word for confusion
following means coming after, so the guns come first and the rest after them
'leader' keeps only the first letter of 'Egypt'

blocks.note: the RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
a mess is a state of confusion
the first letter of Egypt

explanation.surface: An Egyptian king, the country's ruler, is in disarray after the artillery opens fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The RA, Royal Artillery, is the British army's gunners, a crossword staple for guns; Egypt's initial sits between the last two letters of the confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rameses was the name of several kings of ancient Egypt, notably Rameses II, so a pharaoh.

clue.text: Quarry on strike, leaving one open-mouthed

indicators.note: on means attached to, so the quarry is joined onto the strike

blocks.note: to lam is to thrash or hit hard
quarry is a hunted animal, prey

explanation.surface: Workers at a stone quarry go on strike, and one is left gaping in astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarry suggests a stone pit; it is the hunted animal. Open-mouthed is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamprey is a jawless fish with a round sucking mouth that it keeps open to attach itself to prey.

clue.text: About a kilometre in Silverstone

indicators.note: in says the word lies inside the name that follows

blocks.note: the letters run inside this name, after its first three letters

explanation.surface: A lap of the Silverstone motor-racing circuit measures roughly a kilometre.
explanation.walkthrough: Silverstone is the British Grand Prix circuit in Northamptonshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The verst is an old Russian unit of distance of about 1.07 kilometres.

clue.text: Prune tops from prunus: equal part is rare

indicators.note: pruning cuts away growth, and the tops are the leading letters, so the start of each word is cut off

blocks.note: the plum and cherry genus, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction: trim the top growth from the prunus, an equal part being uncommon.
explanation.walkthrough: PR comes off prunus and EQ off equal, leaving UNUS and UAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusual is uncommon or seldom seen, which is what rare means.

clue.text: Led up under tree by first and last painful cry in town

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: the ash is a common tree
taken as written
taken as written, to be read upwards
A and Z, the first and last letters of the alphabet
the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone is led up beneath a tree, crying out in pain, in some town.
explanation.walkthrough: Led up sits under the tree in the grid. ASHBY DE LA ZOUCH is a market town in Leicestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashby-de-la-Zouch is a small English market town, famous from Scott's novel Ivanhoe.

clue.text: Gangster supplies cowl for chimney

blocks.note: a cowl is a monk's hood
lum is the Scots and northern English word for a chimney

explanation.surface: A crook provides the cowl that sits on top of a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: A cowl is also the cap on a chimney, which ties the surface together; LUM is a Scots word for chimney that crosswords lean on.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodlum is a violent criminal, especially one in a gang, so a gangster.

clue.text: Lord right in the underground

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
the maquis was the French Resistance, the wartime underground movement

explanation.surface: A nobleman's place is in the wartime resistance, or on the train beneath London.
explanation.walkthrough: The underground looks like the London Tube, but here it is the secret resistance network in occupied France.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquis is a nobleman ranking above an earl, and addressed as a lord in Britain.

clue.text: Student in rhythm makes animal noise

indicators.note: in places the student inside the word for rhythm

blocks.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
the beat of music is its rhythm

explanation.surface: A music student keeping time produces something like a farmyard sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleat is the cry of a sheep or goat, a typical noise of an animal.

clue.text: What 2s can cause sum bother?

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolchild asks whether some sums might cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 2s refers to the answer at 2 down, PROJECT: things that project stick out like a SORE THUMB. There is no printed signal for the rearrangement; the question mark and 'bother' have to carry it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that projects is said to stick out like a sore thumb, the idiom for being glaringly obvious.

clue.text: Film cat with tentacles gives you pence costs

blocks.note: eight, the number of arms an octopus has
pussy is a familiar word for a cat
surface padding: these words fit no parse and look like a garble in the printed text

explanation.surface: A movie about a many-armed cat that somehow charges you money.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat with tentacles would be an octopus-pussy, the 1983 James Bond film. The closing words 'gives you pence costs' fit no parse and look like a garble in the printed text.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopussy is the 1983 James Bond picture starring Roger Moore, so it is a film title.

clue.text: Held sway with lines

blocks.note: first meaning: governed or was in charge
second meaning: marked with straight lines, like writing paper

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ruler reigning with laws; the second sense is the ruled lines on a page.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb rule means to govern, and paper that has been ruled carries printed straight lines.

clue.text: Get back transport out side the City

indicators.note: outside says one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: to be transported is to be carried away with delight, so a transport is ecstasy
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Recovering the vehicles kept outside the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Transport looks like vehicles; it is a fit of joy. The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapture something is to take it back again, to regain it.

clue.text: Not a crazy wanderer

blocks.note: no, as in 'no fool', means not a
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: Someone who roams about is perfectly sane.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad has no fixed home and moves from place to place, a roaming traveller.

clue.text: Make up mother's a transport first

indicators.note: first tells the solver to place the vehicle ahead of the single letter

blocks.note: ma is mother, plus the possessive s
a car is a means of transport
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mother's cosmetics come before her car.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan shows a stray backslash where the parse needs the word a; transport goes first, ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is cosmetic colouring for eyelashes, a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Entertaining place for American and German compiler in London street

indicators.note: in sets the American and the German self inside the name of the street

blocks.note: US is short for American, as in US forces
the compiler is the setter, who says I, and ich is German for I
the Mall is the avenue running from Trafalgar Square to Buckingham Palace

explanation.surface: A London street is suggested as a venue for American and German crossword setters.
explanation.walkthrough: Compiler means the person who wrote the puzzle, so I, and a German compiler says it in German. The Mall is the grand avenue leading to Buckingham Palace; the insert goes after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A music hall was a theatre for variety shows, a venue for popular entertainment.

clue.text: Stay put, then? — or don't!

blocks.note: surface reading: an instruction to remain where you are
setter's reading: the opposite order, to go away from the spot

explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers an instruction and then cancels it: if you don't stay put, you set off from where you were.
explanation.definitionFit: To move off is to start going away from a place, the reverse of staying where one is.

clue.text: Church managed by Scots? Chew hard!

blocks.note: Sc. is the abbreviation for Scots or Scottish
to have run a business is to have managed it
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Is a church run by Scottish people? A loud order to chew forcefully follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the reverse of clue order: by Scots puts SC first.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrunch is to crunch or crush noisily, as when biting hard into something.

clue.text: Gentleman, formerly, a friend to old city

blocks.note: taken as written
a mate is a friend
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A gentleman of the past was a friend to an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: In English cricket until 1962, unpaid players were called Gentlemen and professionals Players.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket once called unpaid players Gentlemen, so an unpaid sportsman was formerly a gentleman.

clue.text: Buds burst on flower with someone in the cabin

indicators.note: something that has burst is broken apart, so its letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
a flower is something that flows, so a river

explanation.surface: Buds open on a plant belonging to someone in a cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be a bloom alongside the buds; it is a river, the thing that flows. The cabin is the driver's cab of a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus driver sits in the cab at the front of the vehicle, its cabin.

clue.text: Perch, very large, in decay

indicators.note: in puts the size marking inside the word for decay

blocks.note: OS is outsize, the clothing size mark
rot is decay

explanation.surface: A huge fish, a perch, is going rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Perch looks like the fish; it is the place a bird settles.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where birds settle to rest, a perch.

clue.text: Public Library at last in German square

blocks.note: the abbreviation for public library
taken as written
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A public library is at last opened on a German town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' looks like a phrase meaning finally; it splits into AT and the last letter, Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Platz is the German word for a town square or open place, as in Potsdamer Platz.

clue.text: Devilish game taking one to the top?

definitions.text: Devilish game taking one to the top?

blocks.note: surface reading: a wicked pastime or a fiendishly hard contest
setter's reading: a game named after the Italian word for devil, in which a spinning top is tossed and caught on a string

explanation.walkthrough: The top is the spinning toy, not a summit; the game's name comes from the Italian for devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling toy: a double-cone spinning top whirled and thrown up from a string between two sticks.

clue.text: Sort of art in French novel?

blocks.note: first meaning: the word that follows art in the name of the 1890s decorative style
second meaning: the French adjective for novel, that is new

explanation.walkthrough: 'French novel' suggests a book by a French author; novel is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Art nouveau is the decorative style of flowing lines, and nouveau is French for new, a synonym of novel.

clue.text: Sailor belonging to the land, splendid person

blocks.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
of the earth: belonging to the land

explanation.surface: A seaman who is really a landlubber turns out to be a fine fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The salt of the earth is an idiom from the Gospels for a thoroughly good, honest and reliable person.
